textual.context: Instructional walkthrough of an account interface and withdrawal process; the records do not establish whether the earnings or transfer are genuine or completed.
textual.potential_relevance: The claimed mining-related earnings are linked to actions involving a Bitcoin wallet, withdrawal amount, and transfer request, creating a concrete reward-and-asset-transfer relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not verify the platform, wallet ownership, account balance, transaction, recipient, or whether any promised income was actually received.

visual.observation: A BitClub-branded webpage visibly promotes bitcoin-mining earnings and shows an account wallet with a BTC balance and an earnings summary; a separate title card reads “GANA DINERO MINANDO BITCOIN.”
visual.context: Promotional website and title-card context are visible; the frames do not establish whether the claims are independently verified.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible promise of earning bitcoin is linked to the branded mining-pool/account context, creating a reward-and-affiliation relationship that may merit review.
visual.limitations: Sampled frames cannot establish the organization’s identity, legitimacy, actual mining activity, or whether any reward was paid.

visual.observation: The webpage instructs the user to enter and save a Bitcoin payout address, request a withdrawal amount, and provide a security PIN; it also states that withdrawals may take 24–48 hours and references email or Google Authenticator codes.
visual.context: The instructions appear within a visible Bitcoin withdrawal interface and are presented as account-procedure steps.
visual.potential_relevance: A promised bitcoin withdrawal is directly linked to submitting a payout address, withdrawal amount, and authentication code, with stated processing conditions.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether the information was actually submitted, whether funds were transferred, or whether the process was completed.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker explicitly characterizes the transfer as an example and says it will not be performed because the account lacks sufficient funds.

evidence.quote: I'm not gonna do it because you don't have enough money this is nothing more that an example

visual_context_notes.observation: The visible site uses BitClub branding and presents wallet, mining-pool, payout-address, and withdrawal screens.
The final title card uses Spanish promotional wording: “GANA DINERO MINANDO BITCOIN.”

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes making money through BitClub-branded Bitcoin mining and presents displayed account earnings as income generated by miners. It guides viewers through a participation and withdrawal flow involving a Bitcoin payout address, a withdrawal amount, and an emailed security PIN. The example is not completed, so it does not establish that Bitcoin was paid, that the displayed balance was genuine, or what happened to submitted information.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The displayed mining-pool offer links purchasing a pool share to profitability, while the speaker attributes account income to miners. The video then demonstrates where that claimed income could be withdrawn.

evidence.observation: The title presents the video as an earnings-withdrawal walkthrough.

evidence.observation: A BitClub España closing card displays the words “GANA DINERO MINANDO BITCOIN.”
The BitClub page's mining-pool section describes profitability and purchasing a share in a mining pool.
The Bitcoin wallet page displays a BTC balance, a USD value, an earnings summary and a Bitcoin payout-address field.
The withdrawal form displays amount and Bitcoin-address fields, a security-code field, and a Request Bitcoin button.
The speaker says the transfer will not be performed and calls the walkthrough an example.
